title: Why multi-tenant apps need a tenant boundary
items: A multi-tenant app is not just one database with a tenant_id column. The real challenge is enforcing the boundary on every request.
In this project, tenant context is resolved before business logic runs. Regular users cannot switch tenants through a request header.
That check belongs near the request boundary, not scattered across controllers. Centralize the rule, then make services respect the same scope.
The lesson: tenant isolation is an invariant. Treat it like authentication, not as an optional filter added at the end.

title: The first useful lesson from building a modular operations platform
items: One of the first lessons I learned while building a modular operations platform was that navigation is part of authorization.
A sidebar should not merely list every feature in the product. It should reflect the modules enabled for the organization and the permissions available to the current user.
That creates a better user experience, but the UI is only the visible layer. The backend still has to enforce the same rules. Hiding a menu item is not security.
The practical pattern is simple: use shared permission definitions, derive visibility from them, and enforce access again at the API boundary.
Good product architecture makes the allowed path obvious while making the forbidden path impossible.

title: What a good exam player has to protect
items: An online exam player is not just a form with a countdown. It has to protect the attempt, the answers, and the candidate experience at the same time.
The player handles registration validation, camera setup, fullscreen rules, answer syncing, timers, and final submission as one session.
Those concerns should still be separated internally. UI state controls the experience; the API remains the source of truth for the attempt.
The best exam UX feels calm to the candidate because the complex state transitions happen reliably in the background.
